policy: Only source-documented physical objects elevated to owner subjects, unknowns remain zero-link Places; no editorial/photo approvals or original-vs-replica conflations

records.site: Basilica di Santa Cristina, Bolsena
records.principal_documented_physical_subject: Three sacred blood-marked stones associated with the Eucharistic Miracle of 1263 in a gilded wood container in the Chapel of the Sacred Stones; separate fourth sacred stone in polychrome-enamel and metal reliquary c.1940; the sacred corporal is preserved in Orvieto.
records.subject_distinctions: Four distinct stone supports and saint Christina's tomb differ from ORVIETO corporal; no unqualified scientific miracle claim.

records.site: Basilica Papale di Santa Maria degli Angeli in Porziuncola
records.principal_documented_physical_subject: Original medieval Porziuncola chapel inside the dome of the vast Santa Maria degli Angeli Basilica in Assisi; physically distinct from the nearby Chapel of the Transitus and the Rose Garden.
records.subject_distinctions: This is the original small chapel architecture, not the outer basilica or relics of St Francis; 1393 Ilario da Viterbo altarpiece is separate art object.

records.site: Santuario Madonna della Corona
records.principal_documented_physical_subject: Pietà sculptural group venerated at sanctuary carved in Mount Baldo cliff, polychrome local stone relief/sculpture roughly 70×56×25 cm, linked to period of Knights of Malta, not the distant sanctuary facade.
records.subject_distinctions: Local Pietà historical dating to 15th century rather than unverified miraculous transfer from Rhodes in 1522; sanctuary custodian distinguishes earlier Madonna-and-Child fresco.

records.site: Basilica Santuario Maria SS. del Tindari
records.principal_documented_physical_subject: Original venerated dark-wood Madonna-and-Child statue at the Madonna Bruna sanctuary in Tindari, Sicily, with associated 'Nigra sum sed formosa' inscription.
records.subject_distinctions: The sea arrival story is a tradition; the statue exists in sanctuary. Require subject dominance and avoid generic exterior.
